Pseudobulk profiles: aggregate a counts layer over groups of cells

pseudobulk.Rd

Sums (or averages) every feature of a layer over profiles, the combinations of a sample identifier and, optionally, a group label (cell type, condition, cluster). The result is the small features x profiles matrix that pseudobulk differential expression methods (edgeR, DESeq2) consume, together with a table describing each profile.

Usage

pseudobulk(
  object,
  sample_by,
  group_by = NULL,
  ...,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  cells = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  fun = c("sum", "mean")
)

# S3 method for class 'Seurat'
pseudobulk(
  object,
  sample_by,
  group_by = NULL,
  ...,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  cells = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  fun = c("sum", "mean")
)

  cells = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  fun = c("sum", "mean")
)

Arguments

object

A single cell object. Currently, Seurat, SingleCellExperiment, and anndata objects are supported.

sample_by

The sample (biological replicate) of each cell: the name of a metadata column, or a character/factor vector named by cell (one label per cell of the object, or at least per cell in cells). A vector lets a caller aggregate by labels that are not stored in the object.

group_by

Optional group of each cell (same forms as sample_by). With NULL the profiles are the samples themselves.

...

Passed to methods.

assay

Assay / modality to aggregate (default: the default assay of the object; the main modality "X" for AnnData and .h5ad objects).

layer

Layer to aggregate. Defaults to "counts", not to default_layer(): the default layer holds normalised values, which must not be summed. AnnData objects whose raw counts live in X need layer = "X" (or "raw" for adata.raw). An AnnData obsm modality (for example a protein panel) is a single matrix with no layers: pass layer = "X"; any other layer is an error rather than a silent substitution.

cells

A character vector of cell names to include, as they are named in the object (i.e. according to colnames(object)). If NULL, data will be returned for all cells in the object.

features

Features to include (default: every feature of the assay).

fun

"sum" (default) or "mean"; the mean divides each profile's sum by the number of cells that contributed to it.

Value

An object of class scuba_pseudobulk: a list with

  • counts: features x profiles numeric matrix (sums, or means with fun = "mean"),

  • profiles: data.frame with one row per profile (profile_id, sample, group, n_cells), in the column order of counts; group is NA when group_by is NULL,

  • assay, layer, fun, sample_by, group_by (the column names, or NA for vectors),

  • n_cells_dropped: cells left out for a missing sample or group label,

  • engine: "julia", "r" or "python".

Details

The full features x cells matrix is never built: on the Julia engine SCUBA.jl streams the layer into a group accumulator, and on the R engine each matrix class is aggregated with its own block-wise primitive (sparse indicator product for dgCMatrix and dense layers, BPCells::pseudobulk_matrix() for BPCells layers, DelayedArray::colsum() for HDF5-backed layers). AnnData objects (reticulate) are aggregated in cell chunks by a Python helper, in memory or in backed mode.

Cells whose sample or group value is NA or blank are left out (counted in n_cells_dropped). Profiles are ordered sample-major, then by group; levels follow the factor levels of the metadata column when it is a factor, and sorted order (C locale) otherwise, so every engine and backend returns the same columns.

See also

pseudobulk_design() for the metadata-only preview of the profiles, layer_names() to find a counts layer, fetch_matrix().

Examples

pb <- pseudobulk(AML_Seurat, sample_by = "Batch", group_by = "condensed_cell_type")
pb
#> SCUBA pseudobulk: 462 features x 18 profiles (sum of layer 'counts', assay 'RNA', r engine)
#>   samples: 2; groups: 10; cells: 250 (dropped 0)
head(pb$profiles)
#>                                          profile_id   sample           group
#> BM_200AB__B Cells                 BM_200AB__B Cells BM_200AB         B Cells
#> BM_200AB__BM Monocytes       BM_200AB__BM Monocytes BM_200AB    BM Monocytes
#> BM_200AB__CD4+ T Cells       BM_200AB__CD4+ T Cells BM_200AB    CD4+ T Cells
#> BM_200AB__CD8+ T Cells       BM_200AB__CD8+ T Cells BM_200AB    CD8+ T Cells
#> BM_200AB__Dendritic cells BM_200AB__Dendritic cells BM_200AB Dendritic cells
#> BM_200AB__NK Cells               BM_200AB__NK Cells BM_200AB        NK Cells
#>                           n_cells
#> BM_200AB__B Cells              14
#> BM_200AB__BM Monocytes         25
#> BM_200AB__CD4+ T Cells          8
#> BM_200AB__CD8+ T Cells         17
#> BM_200AB__Dendritic cells      15
#> BM_200AB__NK Cells             18
pb$counts[1:3, 1:3]
#>        BM_200AB__B Cells BM_200AB__BM Monocytes BM_200AB__CD4+ T Cells
#> ACTG1                 70                    548                     57
#> ADGRG1                 1                      2                      0
#> AHSP                   0                      0                      0

# Samples only, as means
pseudobulk(AML_SCE(), sample_by = "Batch", fun = "mean")$profiles
#>            profile_id     sample group n_cells
#> BM_200AB     BM_200AB   BM_200AB  <NA>     152
#> PBMC_200AB PBMC_200AB PBMC_200AB  <NA>      98
